## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #14054 automatic session retention - MEDIUM PRIORITY (config + core)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14054 "feat(vscode): reintroduce automatic session cleanup" merged 2026-09-21 implemented backend-owned session retention (legacy extension had auto-cleanup setting, never ported to CLI backend; this brings it back as retention policy in kilo.json with retention.enabled/retention.maxAgeDays fields, enforced server-side via two new kilocode routes: status reads policy + optional last run, run executes pass; deletion happens against shared database with normal cascade, expired roots removed plus follow-up sweep for expired children in other projects; sessions with message/part writes in last hour + everything non-idle in this process held back so tasks running in other windows/TUI survive; drops abandoned-session heuristic entirely, one plain age rule; Run Cleanup Now gated on toggle with confirm dialog, vscode settings gone, extension binds config keys + triggers daily + shows last run; archived sessions included; tests in packages/opencode/test/kilocode/session/retention.test.ts). This is session lifecycle management (config-driven retention policy, backend routes for status/run, daily pass, safety guards for running sessions).

- **Why**: Alexi has session persistence to `~/.alexi/sessions/` (sessionManager.ts) but no lifecycle management (no auto-cleanup, no retention policy, sessions accumulate indefinitely). Users manually delete sessions with `alexi sessions --delete <id>` (src/cli/commands/sessions.ts). A similar retention policy (opt-in via config, age-based expiration, safety guards for running sessions) would keep session storage bounded without manual intervention. Kilocode's approach (backend-owned policy, separate status/run endpoints, daily scheduler in client) is directly portable to Alexi (add retention config to config schema, implement retention pass in sessionManager or new retentionManager module, schedule daily run from CLI or server).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14054 (Kilocode automatic session retention PR, merged 2026-09-21), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi session persistence, no retention), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/commands/sessions.ts (manual delete command)

- **Category**: config + core (retention policy config fields, retention pass implementation in core)

- **Size**: MEDIUM (~1-2 days, ~12-16h). Add retention config schema (retention.enabled, retention.maxAgeDays), implement retention pass (scan sessions dir, filter by age + running status, delete expired with cascade), add safety guards (skip if disabled, hold back sessions with recent writes, never delete running sessions), schedule daily run (CLI startup hook or dedicated scheduler), add manual trigger command (alexi sessions --cleanup), write tests (retention logic + guards).

#### 2. Claude Code #95409 AGENTS.md project-instructions mod - HIGH PRIORITY (core)

- **What**: Claude Code PR #95409 "mods/agents-md: the AGENTS.md project-instructions mod" merged 2026-09-21 implemented AGENTS.md automatic attachment (new project-instructions mod attaches AGENTS.md to turns where engine attaches nothing; Read attaches no nested AGENTS.md where engine attaches nothing to turn; instructionFiles option with legacy key; typings at 2.1.277). This is project-instructions infrastructure (automatic attachment of AGENTS.md to model turns, scoped to turns with no existing attachments, Read tool excludes nested AGENTS.md to avoid duplication).

- **Why**: Alexi already has AGENTS.md at repo root (loaded instructions for agents, seen in system prompt context), but there is no automatic attachment mechanism in orchestrator (agents read AGENTS.md manually or rely on system prompt, no turn-level attachment). Claude Code's approach (automatically attach AGENTS.md to turns where no instructions attached, exclude nested AGENTS.md from Read to avoid duplication) is directly portable to Alexi. This would ensure every turn has project context without manual Read calls and without bloating context with nested duplication. Implementation path: add projectInstructions detection to orchestrator (check for AGENTS.md at project root), attach to turns where no existing project context attached, filter Read tool to exclude nested AGENTS.md paths.

- **Source**: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/95409 (Claude Code AGENTS.md mod, merged 2026-09-21), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/AGENTS.md (existing project instructions), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/orchestrator.ts (orchestrator, no auto-attach), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/read.ts (Read tool, no AGENTS.md filter)

- **Category**: core (orchestrator auto-attach logic)

- **Size**: SMALL (~3-4h). Add projectInstructions detection (check for AGENTS.md / .alexi/rules / .kilocode/rules at project root), implement turn-level attachment (attach to turns where sessionContext has no existing project instructions), add Read tool filter (exclude paths matching AGENTS.md / .alexi/rules when already attached), write tests (auto-attach behavior + Read exclusion).
